A1.justification: Both PDFs describe OOD-Chameleon by the same authors. All 20 pages of v1 and 25 pages of v2, including their appendices, are readable and support comparison of text, equations, tables, and figures.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic, CelebA, and COCO experiments, including algorithm-selection results, ablations, and estimated-attribute experiments in Appendix E.

after.justification: v2 reports original synthetic, vision, and language experiments, with additional ablations, transfer evaluations, ensemble comparisons, and decision-tree analyses in the appendices.

M1.justification: v1's full pairwise-preference selector with Copeland voting is removed; its remaining pairwise descriptor ablations are not that selector. v2 retains regression and multi-label classification, makes the latter the default, and introduces directly trained and MLP-distilled decision-tree selectors. Appendix D.2 also changes the reported real-data MLP from four layers to two.

E1.justification: Synthetic and CelebA coverage remains. COCO evaluation is removed, while MetaShift supplies a different image population for the retained cat/dog and indoor/outdoor task. v2 additionally evaluates OfficeHome object/domain pairs, Colored-MNIST digit/color tasks, CivilComments toxicity classification, and MultiNLI inference, substantially extending both visual coverage and language-task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 removes PPL from the reported selector comparisons, including comparisons where it was v1's strongest vision selector. It adds decision-tree comparisons in Table 5 and uniform ensembling in Table 19. These materially revise the alternatives evaluated, although the five downstream candidate algorithms remain, with logits correction renamed logits adjustment.

E3.justification: The base CelebA collection changes from 1,320 to 720 tasks, with task training sizes restricted from 200–10,000 to 200–1,000; the 4:1 meta-training/test split remains. Fixed single-shift values are replaced by randomly sampled degrees. New protocols include BERT-based language experiments, training and evaluation with average-group error, and training on tasks of at most 1,000 samples before testing on 2,000–3,000 samples.

E4.justification: v2 adds suitability-threshold sensitivity, highest-logit versus random suitable-algorithm selection, and alternative-metric analyses in Appendix E. Appendices I–J add dataset-size extrapolation and detailed decision-tree interpretation and distillation analyses. Existing descriptor-removal, fine-tuning, and inferred-attribute studies remain, although some are relocated or revised.

E5.justification: v1 Table 1 explicitly states that synthetic results average over three seeds. v2 retains the corresponding means and ± values but omits that seed-count disclosure. This is a loss of statistical reporting detail, not evidence that fewer runs were performed.

E6.justification: Many real-data results are replaced: CelebA/ResNet MLC changes from 69.1% selection accuracy and 42.7% worst-group error in v1 Table 2 to 75.0% and 47.7% in v2 Table 2. Revised task generation prevents interpreting these as controlled performance gains or losses. PPL and COCO entries disappear, and extensive new vision, language, and diagnostic results appear. Shared synthetic rows and retained fine-tuning entries remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v2 adds Conjecture 1, explicitly conditioning selector learnability on sufficiently diverse, densely sampled training shifts and generalization within their support. v1 discusses the no-free-lunch motivation without this explicit conjecture. The principal dataset-construction mathematics remains, and no new proof or generalization bound is provided.

C1.justification: The central claim that algorithm selection for OOD generalization is learnable remains. v2 broadens the stated empirical applicability from synthetic and image tasks to language tasks, presents multi-label classification as the principal solution, and promotes the dataset-construction workflow to a released research tool. These extend the contribution statements without replacing the central thesis.

C2.justification: v2 derives concrete algorithm-choice recommendations from decision trees and adds cost-amortization reasoning. It explicitly discusses support-limited generalization, information potentially missed by handcrafted descriptors, binary-class/binary-attribute restrictions, and unaddressed forms of covariate shift. v1's explanation of PPL's advantages disappears. These substantially revise both interpretation and applicability boundaries.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository link and tool-release statement, specifies the fixed suitability threshold and highest-logit inference rule, and reports hidden width 100 for the real-data MLP. It also documents new dataset-construction procedures and the depth-three decision-tree and distillation recipes. These materially expand reproducibility information; the PDFs alone do not verify the linked resource's contents.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting the new datasets, BERT, class balancing, and logit adjustment, including Idrissi, Menon, and Kini, while removing PPL-related references such as Bradley–Terry and Copeland voting. Its positioning relative to algorithm selection, meta-learning, AutoML, and Bell et al. remains broadly intact. Bibliographic publication updates are not treated as new works.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method explanation, and conclusions are extensively rewritten. v2 consolidates algorithm selection in Section 2, gives dataset construction its own Section 3, and organizes experiments by domain and interpretation in Section 4. The appendices are substantially reorganized, including relocation of existing fine-tuning and inferred-attribute material.

P2.justification: v2 changes the main text to two columns, redraws the overview and shift-quantification figures, removes the three-formulation diagram, and replaces the algorithm-difference histogram with a violin plot. Table 1 is transposed and other tables are restructured. New dataset-example displays, diagnostic tables, and decision-tree figures substantially expand the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v1's transfer evidence was concentrated on CelebA and a small COCO evaluation. v2 substantially strengthens the central learnability claim through broader visual transfer and CivilComments-to-MultiNLI evaluation, targeted sensitivity tests, and interpretable decision rules. Clearer limitations and implementation details further improve assessability. Removing the strong PPL comparisons and explicit three-seed disclosure are losses, but the broader validation and diagnostic evidence provide a substantial net improvement. Revised settings do not establish a same-setting performance improvement.
